text: The C. W. Woodworth Award is an annual recognition given by the Pacific Branch of the Entomological Society of America (PBESA) for outstanding achievement in entomology within the Pacific region of the United States over the preceding ten years. This award, which is the PBESA's largest, is named in honor of Charles W. Woodworth and was established on June 25, 1968. It is primarily sponsored by Brian Holden, the great-grandson of Charles W. Woodworth, and his wife Joann Wilfert, with additional support from Dr. Craig W. and Kathryn Holden, and Dr. Jim and Betty Woodworth. A box holding the older records of the PBESA, including likely the names of the first few recipients of the award, is housed in the special collections section of the library at the University of California, Davis.
